description: Default-deny capability for the main window — no fs:, no bare shell:, only core defaults, window management, the narrow dialog:allow-open grant for the project registration folder picker (T-01-02), and a shell:allow-execute grant scoped to exactly one named sidecar binary (plan 02-01, T-02-01/T-02-09) — the renderer itself has no shell capability at all; only the Rust core's own sidecar supervisor (src-tauri/src/sidecar.rs) invokes tauri-plugin-shell, and this scoped grant is what makes that invocation the ONLY process this app's shell permission can ever launch. Tauri v2's ACL/permission system gates PLUGIN commands (dialog:*, core:*, shell:*); this app's own #[tauri::command] handlers are not plugin commands and are exposed solely via main.rs's generate_handler! list, which is the actual default-deny boundary for them — no permissions/ directory defines custom ACL entries for them in this project, so listing them here would have no runtime effect (verified empirically: project_register/project_list/task_create/board_list from plan 01-03 already work without such an entry). Full app-command roster, kept here for auditability since generate_handler! is the enforcement point: project_register, project_list, project_reconcile, project_relocate, task_create, task_update, task_delete, task_set_status, task_reorder, task_set_priority, task_set_estimate, task_set_assignee, epic_create, epic_update, epic_delete, epic_set_status, epic_reorder, epic_set_priority, epic_set_estimate, epic_set_assignee, issue_create, issue_update, issue_delete, issue_reorder, board_list, board_search, actor_list, criterion_create, criterion_update, criterion_toggle, criterion_reorder, criterion_delete, criterion_list, events_activity_trail, events_since_cursor, agent_run_preview, agent_run_start, agent_run_log_window, agent_run_raw_window, agent_runs_for_task, agent_run_acknowledge, worktree_summary, worktree_remove_check, worktree_remove, worktree_recreate, worktree_forget_record, agent_run_stop, agent_run_answer_permission, permission_rules_list, permission_rule_revoke, agent_run_pending_permissions, task_latest_agent_run, board_blocked_summary, board_recovery_summary, agent_runs_pending_orphans, orphan_kill, settings_get, settings_set_credential_mode, settings_store_api_key, settings_clear_api_key, backend_capability_probe, worktree_open, open_command_template, set_open_command_template, git_identifier_resolve, forge_request_for_task, board_forge_flags, settings_set_project_forge, project_forge_overrides, forge_request_draft, forge_open_request, review_files, review_file_patch, review_criteria_state, criterion_check_with_anchor, review_merge_precheck, review_merge_task, forge_epic_request_draft, forge_open_epic_request, forge_request_for_epic, review_epic_task_rollup, board_change_flags, board_epic_progress, review_changes_request_state, review_request_changes, task_file_set_get, task_file_set_set. review_criteria_state (plan 08-02, REVW-03) is read-only: scope + item id in, criteria with anchors and a git-derived staleness verdict out, nothing stored. criterion_check_with_anchor accepts NO sha — the one it stores is the review target's head ref resolved inside the command, so a renderer cannot claim evidence was read at a commit it was not; it refuses a criterion that does not belong to the item and a partial anchor. review_merge_precheck (plan 08-07, REVW-04) is read-only: a task id in, the merge's branches, counts and a side-effect-free will-conflict dry run out, touching no worktree and writing nothing. review_merge_task (plan 08-07, REVW-04) accepts a task id and nothing else, derives every branch and path itself, merges inside a worktree that belongs to the epic (never the task's, never the user's main checkout), is refused by name while another merge into the same epic runs, pushes nothing and writes no status column. board_search (plan 01-08, BOARD-06) is named explicitly here rather than covered by any blanket grant (T-01-02) — free-text search and every filter dimension still run as indexed, parameterised SQL inside packages/core, this command only carries the request/response across the IPC boundary. events_activity_trail/events_since_cursor (plan 01-10, BOARD-09/DATA-05) are both read-only and both cap their requested window server-side (T-01-24) before calling into packages/core. project_reconcile/project_relocate (plan 01-11, BOARD-10/D-16) never enumerate the filesystem and never write board content into a user's repository — project_reconcile re-verifies each project's already-known marker path, project_relocate writes only the identity marker at the user-chosen path after verifying it names the expected project id (T-01-29). agent_run_preview (plan 02-04, D-27/D-28) is read-only — it mutates nothing, creates no worktree and writes no trigger row, so the launch sheet costs nothing until Start Work actually fires. agent_run_start/agent_run_log_window (plan 02-01, AGNT-01/D-04) validate permission_mode against a fixed four-value list, reject an instruction over 4000 characters (plan 02-04, T-02-20), and cap the log window at 100 rows server-side before ever reaching packages/core (T-02-06); agent_run_start (plan 02-09) also resolves the run's credential exactly once per spawn (D-39) and attaches it to the child's environment only, never to argv. agent_run_raw_window (plan 02-07, D-32/T-02-06) is read-only — the raw view's own bounded read over the identical persisted log, returning each line's verbatim text rather than a parsed value, capped server-side at the same 100-row ceiling. agent_runs_for_task/worktree_summary (plan 02-07, 02-UI-SPEC.md "Runs section"/"Worktree summary") are both read-only, bounded reads feeding the item detail panel's two new sections, mutating nothing. agent_run_acknowledge (plan 03-10, D-49) is read-only in effect on everything except a single timestamp column (acknowledged_at), resolves the actor server-side, and is guarded to the abandoned status in its own SQL WHERE clause — acknowledging a non-abandoned run is a no-op and this command can never change a run's status. worktree_remove_check/worktree_remove (plan 03-01, WORK-03/D-41/D-42/D-43) are the worktree-removal surface: worktree_remove_check is a read-only, never-cached git status --porcelain read taken fresh at dialog-open time; worktree_remove resolves the actor server-side and re-reads porcelain itself inside packages/core before ever calling git worktree remove, refusing unconditionally on any uncommitted change — no parameter on this surface, at any layer, can skip that guard. worktree_recreate/worktree_forget_record (plan 03-09, WORK-06/D-45) are D-45's two missing-worktree recovery decisions: both resolve the actor server-side; worktree_recreate recreates a worktree only from the branch and base already recorded on the row and never resolves a new base ref; worktree_forget_record deletes only a database row and makes no filesystem call. agent_run_stop (plan 02-02, PROC-06/D-35) resolves the actor server-side (T-02-13), sends the sidecar's interrupt request and blocks on its ack before writing the run's terminal status, and never touches git — the worktree is left exactly as the agent left it. agent_run_answer_permission (plan 02-05, AGNT-06/D-38) rejects a decision outside allow/deny/allow_always before touching the database, resolves the actor server-side, and relays nothing to the sidecar when the target row is no longer pending. permission_rules_list is read-only; permission_rule_revoke resolves the actor server-side and appends a revocation event. agent_run_pending_permissions/task_latest_agent_run (plan 02-06, AGNT-06) are both read-only — the permission-request card's data source and the item detail panel's own resolution of a task's active run, mutating nothing. board_blocked_summary (plan 02-06, D-37) is read-only — the board's blocked-row indicator and project-rail count read, delegating straight to query::permissions. board_recovery_summary (plan 03-11, D-46) is read-only — the board's Needs Decision pill and project-rail second count-badge read, delegating straight to query::recovery. agent_runs_pending_orphans/orphan_kill (plan 03-06, PROC-05/D-46/D-48) are the launch-time orphan-recovery surface: both resolve the actor server-side (T-01-04), agent_runs_pending_orphans is read-only (it clones the launch classification's own list, populated once at startup, and never re-scans), and orphan_kill signals a process GROUP recorded by this application's own previous run — never a pid supplied by the renderer (T-03-06-03) — rejecting with a not-found error rather than a false success when the named run is no longer pending. settings_get/settings_set_credential_mode/settings_store_api_key/settings_clear_api_key/backend_capability_probe (plan 02-09, D-39) are the credential boundary's command surface — no command in this group ever returns the API key value itself (settings_get reports only whether a key is configured and the date), settings_set_credential_mode validates scope/mode against fixed vocabularies before touching the database, and backend_capability_probe is read-only (it never spawns a session and never touches a credential). git_facts/git_truth_focus_task (Phase 7 plan 07-01, LINK-02/LINK-09) are the git-truth command surface: git_facts is read-only, delegating straight to flywheel_core::git_facts::git_facts_for_task; git_truth_focus_task writes exactly one in-memory AppState field (focused_task) and can never reach the database or the filesystem. worktree_open/open_command_template/set_open_command_template (Phase 7 plan 07-04, LINK-11/D-130) are the worktree-open command surface — the renderer's only route to a process, since the renderer itself holds no shell capability of its own: worktree_open accepts only a task id and one of two enum surfaces, resolves the full argv entirely inside packages/core from a stored template and the task's own worktrees row, and spawns that argv directly with Command::new(argv[0]).args(&argv[1..]) — never a shell, never a joined command line, and no program name, argument or path crosses the IPC boundary from the renderer; open_command_template is a read-only projection of the stored (or default) template for a surface, and set_open_command_template resolves the actor server-side and rejects an empty or whitespace-only template before it is ever stored. git_identifier_resolve (Phase 7 plan 07-05, LINK-04/D-128) is read-only and validates the pasted string against a hex-or-flywheel/-prefix shape before any git invocation (T-07-05-01) — classify runs before the database is ever locked, so an input that is not a plausible hash or branch never reaches a subprocess; a sha is passed to git only as a positional revision argument followed by --, never into a flag position, and the command stores nothing. forge_request_for_task/board_forge_flags/settings_set_project_forge/project_forge_overrides (Phase 7 plan 07-08, LINK-05/LINK-06/LINK-08) are the item panel's/board's forge command surface: forge_request_for_task is a live read that shells out to the user's own already-authenticated gh/glab CLI and returns no credential and no raw CLI stderr (the error category only, T-07-08-01); board_forge_flags is read-only and caps its window server-side before calling into packages/core (T-07-08-04, the board never shells out); settings_set_project_forge validates its forge argument against a fixed three-value vocabulary before touching the database and resolves the actor server-side (T-07-08-02); project_forge_overrides is read-only, the Settings surface's per-project forge select's read half. forge_request_draft/forge_open_request (Phase 7 plan 07-09, LINK-05/D-118) are the board-item-becomes-the-request command surface: forge_request_draft is read-only, assembling and returning the same deterministic draft the preview renders, with no title, no body, no branch and no target accepted as input; forge_open_request accepts only a task id — no title, no body, no branch and no target — so the renderer cannot influence what is published to the forge beyond choosing which task to open a request for, and it writes no status of its own, leaving the In Review move to plan 07-07's single poll-driven edge detector. review_files/review_file_patch (Phase 8 plan 08-01, REVW-01/REVW-02) are the review surface's two read-only commands: both accept a scope (task or epic) and an id, review_file_patch additionally a file path and its pre-rename path, and neither accepts a ref, a sha or a repository path — base, head and repository are derived inside packages/core from the board, and the database lock is released before git runs. forge_epic_request_draft (Phase 8 plan 08-08, REVW-05) is read-only: an epic id in and nothing else, the epic's request draft and the named reason it cannot be proposed yet (if any) out; it accepts no title, body or branch. forge_open_epic_request (plan 08-08, REVW-05) accepts an epic id and nothing else, assembles its own title and body with the same function the draft command uses so the published text is the previewed text, refuses a blocked epic by name, pushes the integration branch with a plain push and no history-rewriting flag, then opens the request, reports a push that landed without a request as its own outcome, never returns raw CLI output, and writes no status column or poll. forge_request_for_epic (plan 08-08) is read-only: an epic id in, the existing request for the epic's integration branch (or none) out. review_epic_task_rollup (plan 08-09, D-132) is read-only: an epic id in and nothing else, each task of the epic out with its current-revision criteria counted as checked-of-total and checked-without-evidence; it spawns no git and writes nothing. board_change_flags (Phase 8.1 plan 01, D-15/D-16) is read-only: a project id in and nothing else, each active worktree of the project out with its commits-ahead count (null when the base cannot be resolved) and a dirty flag; it accepts no path, ref or sha, derives every branch and base inside packages/core, caps its sweep server-side, releases the database lock before git runs, and writes nothing. board_epic_progress (Phase 8.1 plan 05, D-05/D-06) is read-only: a project id in and nothing else, each epic that has tasks plus the no-epic bucket out with its task counts by status, its running and blocked agent-run counts and its criteria position (null when none exist); it spawns no git, caps the roster server-side, and writes nothing. review_changes_request_state (Phase 8.1 plan 21, A-08(a)) is read-only: a task id in and nothing else, whether a decline is ready, already sent back or refused (by a named category) out; it spawns no git and writes nothing. review_request_changes (Phase 8.1 plan 21, A-08(a)) accepts a task id and nothing else, so the renderer cannot supply the reason the agent reads: the reason is the task's unchecked criteria, derived from the board inside packages/core. It writes one task.changes_requested event and moves status by exactly one named edge (to in_progress, through the shared status writer, in the same transaction), takes no status argument and issues no SQL of its own; the forge-driven changes-requested path is a different actor and still moves nothing. task_file_set_get (Phase 9 plan 09-01, PLAN-02/PLAN-04) is read-only: a task id in, the task's declared file-set out. task_file_set_set (Phase 9 plan 09-01, D-148) is HUMAN-ONLY, in the advance_stage family: there is no MCP tool for it and no agent-reachable caller, so an agent can never widen its own scope. It accepts a task id and a list of repo-relative entry strings and nothing else — no actor, no worktree path, no absolute path — resolves the actor server-side, REJECTS rather than repairs any entry that is empty, absolute, carries a parent segment, a doubled separator, a backslash, a control character or a glob character, or names the repository root, stores nothing when any entry is refused (not even the valid ones beside it), caps the list at 200 entries server-side, and writes exactly one task.file_set_declared event in the same transaction as the rows.
